subject.title: Allow before_agent_start hooks to override prompt

question: Should OpenClaw add a user-prompt replacement contract for plugins, and should that contract live on `before_prompt_build` with legacy `before_agent_start` compatibility or on broader LLM interception hooks?
rationale: The requested capability lets enabled plugins alter model-bound user input, so automation should not choose the trust boundary, precedence, filtering, or observability semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add prompt-build replacement
options.body: Add a documented replacement field to `before_prompt_build`, carry it through legacy `before_agent_start`, enforce prompt-injection policy filtering, and cover embedded, CLI, and harness runners.

options.title: Use LLM interception
options.body: Defer this issue to an `llm_input`-style modifying hook if maintainers want prompt rewriting at the provider boundary instead of the prompt-build boundary.

options.title: Reject prompt replacement
options.body: Keep plugin prompt hooks additive-only and direct oversized-prompt mitigation to context-engine, memory, or provider-side controls.

recommendation.title: Add prompt-build replacement
recommendation.body: Add a documented replacement field to `before_prompt_build`, carry it through legacy `before_agent_start`, enforce prompt-injection policy filtering, and cover embedded, CLI, and harness runners.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent history across the shared hook contracts and prompt hook seam extraction needed for a cross-runner API decision.
